endonym.native: Principatele Unite ale Moldovei și Țării Românești

capsule: The United Principalities emerged from the dual election of Alexandru Ioan Cuza as prince of both Moldavia and Wallachia in January 1859, a maneuver that exploited the Paris Convention of 1858 to achieve de facto Romanian unification without great-power opposition. Cuza enacted land reform and secularization of monastic estates before being forced to abdicate in 1866; the principalities then invited the Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen prince Carol to rule, and in 1866 formally renamed the state Romania. Full independence from Ottoman suzerainty was recognized at the Congress of Berlin in 1878, and Romania became a kingdom in 1881.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political history and boundaries of the United Principalities are well documented in diplomatic records; the to-date of 1917 reflects dataset conventions for the Romanian state's continuity through World War I.
